claims.text: Trench sample NR016 7.76% Li2O on a spodumene ('spd') zone
claims.status: 7.76% Li2O is close to pure spodumene (~8.0%) – a selective mineral sample, not a grade

claims.text: Diamond-drill core NDDH-004 box 9 logged with spodumene at ~29–31 m
claims.status: Visual logging only – assays not shown

claims.text: Saurimo diamond cluster: 650,000 ct/yr installed; 'actual realized production 448 carats (69%)'

claims.text: Namibe dimension-stone cluster: ~US$104.9 M, completion 2026, ~32 km from Moçâmedes with road, rail and port connections

claims.text: Chipindo: 66 holes (~8,370 m); of 1,458 ALS samples 104 ≥0.5 g/t and 50 ≥1 g/t Au; best 7.33 g/t (TC_012, 94–95 m), 7.22 g/t (CS009), 6.64 g/t (TC_019)

claims.text: LAFECH channels reach 19.5 g/t (Tchambassuco) and 15.8 g/t (Chiriva)

claims.text: Chipindo concession memo reports ≈20% monazite–xenotime in alluvial heavy-mineral concentrates

claims.text: Chipindo associated minerals: pyrite (297 intervals), chalcopyrite (276), arsenopyrite (16), sphalerite (7), visible gold (5); As to 6,950 ppm; Cu max 450 ppm

claims.text: Cambuta oval magnetic intrusion with Cu–As anomalies → possible porphyry/skarn Cu–Au target
claims.status: Hypothesis only

claims.text: Lombige: Mn layer averaging ≈49% Mn, 0.7 m thick; historic alluvial gold production 3.3 kg (1943–44); title expired on its face in 2022
claims.status: Tenure blocker

claims.text: Alto Zambeze (Mexico/Moxico): six grab samples 25–26% Cu, Ag, Au in two; laboratory certificates state the sample source was not verified
claims.status: Measured value, unverified provenance

claims.text: Namibe coast: 75 recorded mineral sites incl. 35 copper (3 ocorrências, 32 indícios), 21 marble quarries, 5 gypsum, 3 Mn; nine zones Z1–Z9 drawn 2.5 km around occurrences

candidates.name: Chipindo gold district (P1, with Chimbumbula P7)
candidates.tenure: Held – S2 scores tenure 2/2 from title copies; not checked on cadastre
candidates.hypothesis: Orogenic, shear-hosted quartz–sulphide gold along a NE–SW Cassanda–Tchiquele corridor, shedding the alluvial gold that has been worked in 27 zones.
candidates.strongest: Drilling: 50 of 1,458 ALS samples ≥1 g/t, best 7.33 g/t over 1 m (TC_012), with independent LAFECH channels to 19.5 g/t on the same corridor.
candidates.competing: A nuggety, narrow-vein system whose high surface values (TR-009 ≈16 g/t over 4 m) come from supergene enrichment and do not persist – i.e. small-scale/alluvial economics only.
candidates.gap: No QA/QC (certified standards, blanks, duplicates), no down-hole surveys or structural orientation, no continuity model; REE claim not in the database.
candidates.test: Obtain ALS certificates + QA/QC + collar/down-hole surveys (R04); re-log 10 key holes and send 5% of pulps to an umpire lab; cross-section the 7 best intercepts. ≈US$25–40 k, 6–8 weeks.
candidates.advance: QA/QC passes (CRM bias <5%, umpire repeat within ±10%) AND ≥3 holes show ≥3 m @ ≥2 g/t on one structure over ≥400 m strike → first drill budget (≈US$1–1.5 M step-out/infill).
candidates.defer: Data reproduce but intercepts are isolated (<1.5 m, no continuity) → hold; option on alluvial/small-scale only.
candidates.stop: Umpire assays fail (>15% low bias) or certificates cannot be produced → stop spend.

candidates.name: Longonjo NdPr carbonatite (Ozango Minerals / Pensana)
candidates.tenure: Mining licence 21 km² (S1 site plan); JORC Ore Reserve published by operator (S4)
candidates.hypothesis: Weathered carbonatite REE deposit (monazite-rich regolith over carbonatite) – an advanced development project, not an exploration target.
candidates.strongest: Operator JORC Ore Reserve: 21.54 Mt @ 3.04% TREO, 0.65% NdPr (S4) – the only code-compliant estimate among the critical-mineral projects reviewed.
candidates.competing: Not a geological competitor: the risk is that government figures (120 kt/yr NdPr oxide, US$90 M capex, US$250 M/yr) overstate scale – the entire reserve holds ~139 kt NdPr.
candidates.gap: Independent technical review, metallurgical recoveries, offtake and funding status; reconciliation of S1 vs S4 figures.
candidates.test: Request the Ore Reserve report, JORC Table 1 and metallurgical test-work summary (R07); one desk reconciliation by an independent CP. ≈US$15–25 k.
candidates.advance: Reserve and recoveries reconcile; capex funded; product spec (MREC) acceptable to target offtaker → proceed to transaction diligence.
candidates.defer: Funding gap or offtake unsettled → monitor.
candidates.stop: Material reserve downgrade or licence dispute.

candidates.name: Bonga niobium–phosphate carbonatite (NioBonga)
candidates.tenure: S1: pilot mining. Not in S2 title list – confirm licence type and area (R05)
candidates.hypothesis: Pyrochlore-bearing carbonatite (Nb ± REE, apatite P) with a laterite/eluvial cap – the only niobium site in either dataset.
candidates.strongest: USGS records a Nb–Ta carbonatite deposit and UTE-4 radiometrics show a strong Th–U high over ≈39 km² (two different families: F-USGS and F-AIR).
candidates.competing: Barren or Nb-poor carbonatite/alkaline plug: Th–U highs also arise from monazite-only or fenite; 'pilot mining' may be phosphate/iron only.
candidates.gap: No Nb2O5 grade anywhere; no resource; whole-rock Nb in surrounding rocks is background (≤88 ppm). Operator product list ('aluminium powder') is geologically unexplained.
candidates.test: Request pilot-mining assays and any drill data (R06). If none: 40–60 rock/soil samples by lithium-borate fusion ICP-MS (Nb, Ta, REE, P) + handheld spectrometer traverse. ≈US$20–30 k.
candidates.advance: ≥0.5% Nb2O5 over coherent zones (≥200 m) or ≥1% TREO in regolith → drill budget.
candidates.defer: Nb 0.1–0.5% Nb2O5 – sub-economic alone; revisit for P/REE by-product.
candidates.stop: Nb2O5 <0.1% and TREO <0.5% across the carbonatite.

candidates.name: Namibe lithium pegmatites (AngoLítio / Tyranna)
candidates.tenure: Prospecting title 023/05/03/T.P/ANG-MIREMPET 2023 (S1); separate from Telhabel title 025/05/05/T.P in S2
candidates.hypothesis: LCT (lithium–caesium–tantalum) spodumene pegmatite swarm in Namibe basement.
candidates.strongest: Spodumene identified in drill core NDDH-004 (29–31 m) and grabs to 4.24% Li2O on a georeferenced operator map (S1 slide 18).
candidates.competing: Isolated, thin pegmatite pods with high-grade selective grabs (NR016 7.76% is near-pure spodumene) – tonnage insufficient.
candidates.gap: Drill assays and intercept widths, certificates/QA-QC, pegmatite geometry, mineral speciation (spodumene vs petalite/lepidolite), Fe content.
candidates.test: Retrieve Tyranna ASX releases with JORC Table 1 and drill assays (R09) – free, 1 day. Then a 2-day field visit to verify outcrop widths and resample 10 sites with chain of custody (≈US$15 k).
candidates.advance: ≥5 drill intercepts ≥10 m @ ≥1% Li2O, open along strike → partnership / budget discussion.
candidates.defer: Narrow (<5 m) or low-grade intercepts → hold.
candidates.stop: Drilling shows pods <2 m and grabs not reproducible.

candidates.name: Alto Zambeze copper (P3, Sofricangol)
candidates.hypothesis: Copperbelt-analogue sediment-hosted or vein copper on the Angolan side of the Central African Copperbelt trend.
candidates.strongest: Six grab samples at 25–26% Cu with laboratory certificates (S2) – but the laboratory states the sample source was not verified.
candidates.competing: Hand-picked malachite float or artisanal ore of unknown origin; a vein showing, not a stratiform system.
candidates.gap: Sample provenance, geology map, any systematic soil/stream data; area falls in PLANAGEO 'Região Leste' still being surveyed.
candidates.test: Chain-of-custody field visit: 25 rock chips + 15 stream sediments + mapping of the grab sites (≈US$40–60 k incl. logistics).
candidates.advance: Re-sampling reproduces ≥2% Cu in outcrop over ≥50 m or stream anomalies ≥5× background over ≥3 km → soil grid + IP.
candidates.defer: Only float/vein material found → hold until PLANAGEO Leste data released.
candidates.stop: No copper found at the reported sites.

domains: Domain 6 – Archean Block (base metals, gold and diamonds)

candidates.name: Namibe coastal copper zones (Z1, Z4, Z5; P4 Tômbua–Virei, P6 Pedra Grande)
candidates.prec: occurrence layer ±250 m; zones by construction
candidates.holder: P6 application (Pedra Grande); P4 Tômbua–Virei holder per S2; remainder unknown
candidates.tenure: P6 is an application; P4 outline from a small location map – verify all on cadastre
candidates.hypothesis: Fault- and contact-controlled copper veins in Proterozoic granites/metasediments, locally linked to Aptian rift volcanism.
candidates.strongest: Malachite on a fault through Tangalala metasediments at Bacati with old prospecting pits and a 2019 field station logging malachite (Z4).
candidates.competing: Small vein showings with no bulk-tonnage potential – consistent with all ~40 whole-rock samples at background (Cu ≤105 ppm).
candidates.gap: No assays at any of the 35 copper sites; no geophysics at prospect scale.
candidates.test: 5-day mapping + 60 rock chips across Z4 and Z1 with portable XRF and lab confirmation (≈US$20–30 k).
candidates.advance: ≥1% Cu over continuous ≥100 m structures, or a coherent soil anomaly ≥300 m → IP survey.
candidates.stop: Rock chips <0.3% Cu across mapped structures.

candidates.name: Lombige gold–manganese (P2)
candidates.holder: Per S2 – title expired on paper 2022
candidates.hypothesis: Supergene Mn oxide layer plus orogenic-source alluvial gold in the West Congo belt.
candidates.strongest: Sampled Mn layer averaging ≈49% Mn over 0.7 m; 3.3 kg historic alluvial gold (1943–44).
candidates.competing: Thin Mn layer of limited lateral extent; gold historically exhausted.
candidates.gap: Valid tenure; Mn layer extent; Fe/P/SiO2 impurities.
candidates.test: Cadastre search at ANRM (R05) – cost ≈US$0–2 k, 2 weeks. Nothing else should be spent first.
candidates.advance: Title valid or re-applicable → 10-pit Mn sampling programme.
candidates.stop: Area re-granted to a third party.

candidates.name: Mavoio-Tetelo copper (Shining Star Icarus)
candidates.tenure: Not in S2; verify licence type
candidates.hypothesis: Historic hydrothermal / sediment-hosted Cu (USGS 'Tetelomavajo Tetelo' hydrothermal deposit) in West Congo belt carbonates.
candidates.strongest: Core photographs of hematite–chalcocite with native copper (S1 slide 15) at a site the USGS also lists as a known copper deposit.
candidates.competing: High-grade but small historic orebody; production figures conflate ore throughput with concentrate.
candidates.gap: Any resource, drill database, metallurgical recovery; S1 slide has internal contradictions (deposit type, dates).
candidates.test: Request resource/feasibility documents and drill database (R10); verify licence on cadastre.
candidates.defer: Resource absent but drilling data credible.

candidates.name: Cácata phosphate & fertilizer plant (Minbos)
candidates.prec: ≈5 km (inset; 45 km NE of Cabinda City)
candidates.hypothesis: Sedimentary marine phosphorite in the Cabinda coastal basin (Cretaceous–Tertiary).
candidates.strongest: Operator DFS and construction contract (S6) and USGS 'Cabinda phosphate – feasibility 2017' (S2d).
candidates.competing: Small-scale, regional-market product with limited export upside.
candidates.gap: Resource statement, P2O5 grade, Cd/U contents, plant naming discrepancy (Subatando vs operator name).
candidates.test: Retrieve ASX resource + DFS (R08); confirm offtake and permits.
candidates.advance: Resource and DFS reconcile with S1 capacity (50→300 kt/yr).

candidates.name: Kassinga iron ore & steel (Tosyali)
candidates.hypothesis: Banded-iron-formation hosted iron ore (Cassinga) with supergene enrichment.
candidates.strongest: Known historic deposits (USGS Cassinga North and South).

candidates.name: Kassala-Kitungo iron ore (Capital Mining)
candidates.gap: 6 Mt/yr for US$27 M is not credible without a resource.

candidates.name: Lulo and Chiri kimberlite projects (Lucapa; Rio Tinto)
candidates.prec: Lulo: USGS U30 ±10 km; Chiri: province only
candidates.hypothesis: Kimberlite pipes feeding the Lucapa-graben alluvial fields.
candidates.strongest: Chiri systematic core-drilling grid and bulk-sample trench plan (S1 slide 13).
candidates.gap: Diamonds are outside the critical-minerals mandate.

candidates.name: Cunene Complex Ni–Cu–(PGE) – Domain 3
candidates.holder: Unknown – no titles in either source
candidates.tenure: Open on available evidence – cadastre not checked
candidates.hypothesis: Magmatic Ni–Cu–PGE sulphide in mafic–ultramafic phases of the Cunene anorthosite complex.
candidates.strongest: S1 critical-mineral map plots a cluster of Ni+Co+Cu+Cr occurrences inside the 'Cunene Complex (base metals–Ni–PGE)' airborne domain (independent families: F-OCC vs F-AIR).
candidates.competing: Fe–Ti–V oxide (massif-anorthosite) mineralisation, or Ni–Co in laterite over ultramafics – neither gives a sulphide Ni–Cu–PGE system.
candidates.gap: No assays, no occurrence descriptions, no stream geochemistry; occurrence positions only from a slide.
candidates.test: Data request to IGEO for the occurrence register + UTE-1/2/6 stream-sediment geochemistry and airborne XYZ (R01, R02). Desk targeting of magnetic/gravity highs on ultramafic units. ≈US$10–20 k of analysis.
candidates.advance: Records show sulphide (pentlandite/pyrrhotite) or Ni >0.3% in rock; coincident magnetic high on ultramafic → reconnaissance field visit.
candidates.defer: Only oxide/laterite records → reframe as Fe–Ti–V or Ni laterite.
candidates.stop: Register shows the Ni–Co points are historic mentions with no rock.

domains: Domain 3 – Cunene Complex (base metals, nickel + PGEs)

candidates.name: East of Lubango Th-high / K-low radiometric area (Z11)
candidates.hypothesis: Unmapped alkaline intrusions / carbonatite with REE–Nb, analogous to Bonga 35 km north.
candidates.strongest: ≈201 km² of high-Th / low-K airborne response (UTE-4) in the same district as the Bonga Nb carbonatite.
candidates.competing: Lateritic weathering concentrating Th in resistate minerals over ordinary granite – the commonest cause of such a response.
candidates.gap: No ground check; geology outside the 1:250k sheet used by S2.
candidates.test: 2-day ground traverse with handheld gamma spectrometer + 30 soil/rock samples by fusion ICP-MS (≈US$10–15 k).
candidates.advance: Alkaline/carbonatite rocks found or TREO >0.3% in rock → systematic sampling.

domains: Domain 3 – Cunene Complex (base metals, nickel + PGEs)

candidates.name: SE Angola 'Copper Belt' domain under Kalahari cover – Domain 1
candidates.tenure: Open on available evidence; protected areas visible on S1 slide 4 overlap the south
candidates.hypothesis: Extension of Katangan/Lufilian Copperbelt stratigraphy beneath Kalahari sand.
candidates.strongest: Interpreted as 'Copper Belt' from airborne magnetics (S1 slide 6); the few digitised occurrences inside it sit in the Cazombo salient at its northern edge, not under the Kalahari-covered core.
candidates.competing: Domain boundaries reflect magnetic texture of cover/basement, not Katangan host rocks; cover depth may be >100 m.
candidates.gap: No occurrence points in the Kalahari-covered core of the domain on S1 slide 9; PLANAGEO Leste survey not concluded; cover thickness unknown; parks.
candidates.test: Defer: request the Leste airborne data and any water-bore logs for cover depth (R02, R11).
candidates.advance: Data show shallow cover (<50 m) and Katangan-like magnetic stratigraphy.
candidates.defer: Default until Leste data are released.
candidates.stop: Cover >150 m or area inside protected zones.

candidates.name: Cabinda / Mayombe gold – Domain 9
candidates.hypothesis: Orogenic gold in the Mayombe (West Congo) belt, continuing the Maiombe alluvial-gold belt (Buco-Zau).
candidates.strongest: Au+Ag occurrence symbols plotted in Cabinda on S1 slide 9 inside the 'Cabinda (gold)' domain; S2 rates Cabinda gold 'probable-high'.
candidates.competing: Alluvial-only gold from distal sources; heavy forest cover limits outcrop.
candidates.test: Data request R01 (Cabinda subset) + stream-sediment BLEG data if any; then a reconnaissance stream survey (≈US$30–40 k).
candidates.advance: Primary occurrences (veins) recorded or stream BLEG ≥10 ppb clusters.

candidates.name: West Congo belt Cu–Pb–Zn–V (Uíge / Zaire)
candidates.hypothesis: Sediment-hosted Cu and carbonate-hosted Pb–Zn(–V vanadate) in West Congo Supergroup carbonates.
candidates.strongest: Clustered Cu+Co+Au+Pb+Zn, Pb+Cu+Zn and Zn symbols (S1 slide 9) around USGS deposits Lueca (V–Pb) and Tetelo (Cu).
candidates.competing: Small oxidised showings with vanadate only near surface.
candidates.test: R01 register subset + historical reports for Lueca/Tetelo; desk review (≈US$5–10 k).
candidates.advance: Historic grades ≥3% Zn+Pb or ≥1% Cu over mappable horizons.

candidates.name: Moxico Archean / Proterozoic Cu–Ni–Au (Domains 6–7)
candidates.hypothesis: Greenstone-hosted Au and Cu–Ni in Archean/Proterozoic basement windows.
candidates.strongest: Au+Ag occurrence cluster near the eastern border (S1 slide 9) inside Domains 6–7.
candidates.competing: Domain labels are interpretive; sparse outcrop.
candidates.gap: Leste region survey incomplete; no assays.
candidates.test: Combine with E05 field visit logistics; request Leste data (R02).

domains: Domain 7 – Proterozoic Orogeny (copper, nickel and gold)

candidates.name: Namibe coastal heavy-mineral placers (Z9)
candidates.hypothesis: Pleistocene beach/terrace placers of ilmenite–magnetite sourced from the Cunene basic suites.
candidates.strongest: Only dark heavy-mineral laminae in older quartzites are mentioned – no placer record.
candidates.test: 10 auger holes / pan concentrates along terraces (≈US$8 k).
